space.origin: feet centre, y = 0, same actor origin used by src/render/target.ts
space.axisNote: Vertices are exported as (x, y, -z), matching src/render/scene.ts target drawing.

nodes.enemy-root: fall pivot at the feet; death rotates this node
nodes.spine: waist pivot; breathing, hit flinch and fire reaction
nodes.head: neck pivot; look and hit flinch
nodes.weapon: rifle group; fire kick; no magazine node

clips.name: walk
clips.source: original two-step loop; hip swing 0.38 rad forward / 0.30 rad back

clips.name: fire
clips.source: original 120 ms reaction performance; the runtime muzzle flash is 65 ms in src/render/weapon.ts, not this clip's length

clips.name: death
clips.source: src/render/feedback.ts fall ramp to 0.47 pi in 600 ms

actions.name: fire
actions.notes: Presentation only; bot accuracy and fire cadence stay in src/sim/bot.ts.

actions.name: reload
actions.notes: Bots emit reload at src/sim/bot.ts:66 and :75. The enemy mesh has no separate magazine node, so no reload clip is claimed; adding one requires splitting the weapon mesh first.

actions.name: crouch
actions.notes: src/render/target.ts squashes height to 0.65; the exported mesh keeps the standing pose.

gaps: Rigid groups are not a skin: elbows, knees and the rifle grip do not deform, and the arms keep the source aiming pose.
Walk and death are node-level approximations; foot contact and silhouette need the real game view with the courtyard lighting.
The source weapon geometry is inside the body mesh; a real reload needs the rifle and magazine split into their own nodes.
No in-game GPU roster or side-by-side comparison exists yet; this file does not claim final quality.
